stories.original: **Mastercard explores selling Vocalink back to UK banks** *A potential divestiture of the UK's core payments infrastructure operator would reshape the ownership landscape just as Britain builds a new domestic scheme.* Mastercard is examining the case for selling Vocalink, the platform that processes Faster Payments, Bacs and LINK transactions in the UK, according to the Financial Times. The company acquired Vocalink from a consortium of British banks in 2016 for around £700 million, and the review comes as Europe's instant payments mandate reduces the strategic differentiation that batch and legacy clearing infrastructure once offered. The timing is driven by several converging forces. The UK Payments Initiative, launched in June as a domestic alternative to card scheme dominance, is building momentum with participants such as GoCardless and Moneyhub already on board. Selling Vocalink back to UK banks would align with the broader sovereignty argument that has animated European payments policy this year, from Visa's €500 million pledge to EPI's expansion across five markets. For Mastercard, the calculus appears to be whether Vocalink's role in legacy clearing infrastructure justifies continued ownership as real-time account-to-account rails gain ground. For UK banks, reacquiring Vocalink would give them direct control over critical national payments infrastructure at a moment when the industry is actively debating who should own and operate the next generation of domestic rails. *Sources: [Mastercard examines sale of Vocalink - FT](https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48079/mastercard-examines-sale-of-vocalink---ft?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra | [Vocalink's Future Turns on Europe's Faster Payments Shift | PYMNTS.com](https://www.google.com/url?rct=j&sa=t&url=https://www.pymnts.com/cryptocurrency/2026/vocalink-future-turns-europe-faster-payments-shift/&ct=ga&cd=CAIyGjQ2YzdlNzNlYWNlZDg4ZTE6Y29tOmVuOlVT&usg=AOvVaw3HvYnDPv7OMJYQFTYvnCbA) — Google Alert — instant payments Europe*

**UK chancellor announces open finance push focused on SME lending**

*The government plans to consult on extending open finance to small business lending, a concrete policy step beyond the FCA's broader 2030 roadmap.*

The UK chancellor has announced plans to accelerate open finance development, with an initial focus on SME lending. The government intends to consult on measures that would allow lenders to access richer financial data from small businesses, with the aim of unlocking billions in additional credit.

This moves open finance from regulatory aspiration to active government policy. The FCA published its open finance roadmap in April with a 2030 target and investment data in scope, but that framework left the question of sectoral priorities largely open. By identifying SME lending as the first application, the Treasury is signalling where it sees the most immediate economic return from broader data sharing.

For banks and fintechs operating in business lending, the consultation will be the key document to watch. The practical questions, such as which data categories are in scope, whether participation will be mandatory and how liability for data quality is allocated, will determine whether this becomes a genuine catalyst for competition in SME finance or another framework that takes years to operationalise.

*Sources: [Chancellor to Unlock Billions for Small Businesses - Mirage News](https://www.google.com/url?rct=j&sa=t&url=https://www.miragenews.com/chancellor-to-unlock-billions-for-small-1708966/&ct=ga&cd=CAIyGjgzMWYyODgyNDEyNDM0NTc6Y29tOmVuOlVT&usg=AOvVaw3UVXZo1BAUJe90Ogyuky4I) — Google Alert — open finance*

stories.original: **PayPal's European payments push lifts investor sentiment** *PayPal's renewed focus on instant payments, fraud prevention and consumer experience across Europe is being read by markets as a strategic repositioning after the company shut its venture arm and joined the European Payments Council.* PayPal shares rose as the company's European payments strategy and an index reshuffle lifted market sentiment. The company's focus on instant payments, fraud prevention and consumer payment experiences across Europe appears to be gaining traction with investors following a period of restructuring under its new chief executive. The trajectory is notable when set against PayPal's recent moves. The company joined the European Payments Council in early July, shut down its venture capital arm in June, and has been repositioning itself as an infrastructure player rather than a consumer brand. Its European push comes as the continent's instant payments mandate creates new competitive dynamics, with incumbents and challengers alike forced to upgrade their real-time capabilities. For European payments professionals, the question is whether PayPal can carve out a meaningful role in a market where Wero, UKPI and domestic account-to-account schemes are all competing for the same transaction volumes. PayPal's scale and brand recognition give it advantages that pure-play open banking providers lack, but its historically card-funded model sits uneasily alongside the account-to-account rails that European policy is actively promoting. *Sources: [PayPal rises as Europe payments push and index reshuffle appear to lift sentiment](https://www.google.com/url?rct=j&sa=t&url=https://www.quiverquant.com/news/PayPal%2Brises%2Bas%2BEurope%2Bpayments%2Bpush%2Band%2Bindex%2Breshuffle%2Bappear%2Bto%2Blift%2Bsentiment&ct=ga&cd=CAIyGjQ2YzdlNzNlYWNlZDg4ZTE6Y29tOmVuOlVT&usg=AOvVaw1rDQOVS3bLzEn6E2vXXYGL) — Google Alert — instant payments Europe*

**Nopan raises €7.2 million to tackle open banking payment reliability**

*The startup, founded by former Netflix engineers, is targeting the conversion and reliability gap that continues to hold back pay-by-bank adoption at scale.*

Nopan has raised €7.2 million from Newion and Seedcamp to build optimisation technology for bank and wallet payments. The company, founded by former Netflix engineers, is focused on improving the reliability and conversion rates of open banking payment flows, a persistent weakness that has limited merchant adoption despite growing regulatory support.

Payment reliability remains one of the most stubborn barriers to pay-by-bank scaling. While open banking transaction volumes have grown substantially, conversion rates still lag behind card payments due to inconsistent bank API performance, variable authentication flows and dropout during redirect sequences. Nopan's bet is that the same kind of performance engineering that Netflix applied to video streaming can be applied to payment initiation.

The raise is modest by fintech standards, but it targets a specific infrastructure gap rather than another front-end proposition. As schemes such as Wero and UKPI build out their reach, the middleware layer that ensures payments actually complete reliably becomes increasingly important. Whether Nopan can build a defensible position in this layer will depend on whether it can access enough transaction data across banks and markets to train its optimisation models effectively.

*Sources: [The ex-Netflix duo on a mission to close the reliability gap in Europe's bank and wallet payments](https://www.google.com/url?rct=j&sa=t&url=https://techfundingnews.com/nopan-raises-7-2m-ex-netflix-open-banking-payments/&ct=ga&cd=CAIyGjVmNjkxZDEzNTU2NWU1MTc6Y29tOmVuOlVT&usg=AOvVaw1ehvGBOq_PwAFUbl60-uPP) — Google Alert — open banking*
